Chevron completed the acquisition of Hess Corporation, an independent oil and gas exploration and production company, on July 18, 2025 [1].
The aggregate purchase price of Hess was approximately $48 billion, which included open market purchases of Hess common stock and Chevron common stock issued as closing consideration [2].
As a result of measuring the acquired assets and assumed liabilities at fair value, there was no goodwill or bargain purchase recognized [2].
Chevron notes that the success of the acquisition depends on realizing anticipated benefits, including run-rate cost synergies, production and free cash flow growth rates, and long-term shareholder returns [3].
However, the acquisition may also present operational challenges, integration risks, or potential legal liabilities related to Chevron's control of the general partner of Hess Midstream LP [3][4].

citations.quote: On July 18, 2025, the company acquired Hess Corporation (Hess), an independent oil and gas exploration and production company.

The aggregate purchase price of Hess was approximately $48 billion, including 15.38 million shares of Hess common stock purchased in open market transactions in the first quarter of 2025 and 301.25 million shares of Chevron common stock issued as closing consideration in July.

The success of the acquisition of Hess, which closed in July 2025, will depend, in part, on Chevron’s ability to realize the anticipated benefits, including the anticipated run-rate cost synergies, estimated five-year production and free cash flow growth rates, and anticipated higher returns to shareholders over the long-term.

Our control of the general partner of Hess Midstream may increase the possibility that we could be subject to claims of breach of duties owed to Hess Midstream, including claims of conflict of interest.
